title: Postcard and Letters
premise: Ten years ago, cellist Casper Kavanagh walked off a stage mid-concert and out of the life he shared with violinist Ilse Marchetti, choosing silence over confession. When a snowstorm traps him in an Alpine inn with Ilse and her fiancé, conductor Theo Brandt—the two rivals of his youth—he can no longer hide behind duty and distance. Over three snowbound days, old letters and unsent postcards surface, forcing each of them to admit what survival cost them. Casper finally speaks the sentence he rehearsed for a decade, but Ilse must choose between the safe future she built and the love she buried; she chooses Casper, not as an escape from her life, but as a return to herself.
about_author: Astrid Nystrom is a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years touring with chamber ensembles before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in the spaces where music, memory, and regret collide, and lives above a bookshop in Bergen with a temperamental cat named Adagio.

chapters.title: The Last Note Nobody Heard
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A decade after his catastrophic final performance, Casper teaches cello in obscurity, keeping a shoebox of unsent postcards addressed to Ilse. When an invitation arrives for a memorial concert honoring their late mentor, he almost burns it—then packs the box instead. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One Mountain
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse boards the funicular to the Alpine inn with her fiancé Theo, rehearsing the speech where she'll ask Casper to play cello at the memorial. She tells herself it's professional courtesy, not unfinished business. Emotional beat: controlled anticipation, a woman who has organized her life around one absence.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm closes the pass; the inn's generator fails; candles and cheap wine. Casper walks into the lobby and finds Ilse and Theo already there. Ten years collapse into one held breath. Emotional beat: shock curdling into forced civility as the three sit down to dinner neither rival nor friend.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sent to fetch wine, Theo discovers a crate of the mentor's belongings—including letters revealing the mentor knew about Casper and Ilse all along, and chose them both for the same quartet knowing it would break. Emotional beat: Theo's quiet devastation as he realizes he may have been the safe choice, not the loved one.

chapters.title: Duet in a Dark Room
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Power still out, Ilse finds Casper playing by candlelight in the music room—the piece they never finished. She picks up a violin left behind by a guest. They play once, badly, then perfectly. Emotional beat: dangerous tenderness, muscle memory of the heart outrunning judgment.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback braided with present: why Casper fled—his father's ruin, the debt, the offer that required leaving everything, including her. He'd told himself disappearing was protection. Now, watching Ilse laugh at Theo's jokes, he understands it was cowardice wearing duty's coat. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Theo's Gambit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts Casper on the frozen terrace—not with fists but with the mentor's letter, offering it like a grenade with the pin pulled. 'She deserves someone who stays,' he says, 'and I need to know if that's me.' Emotional beat: dignity under siege; a rival becoming the story's most honest man.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsent
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The storm breaks; departure looms. Ilse finds the shoebox Casper left in the music room—ten years of postcards, each ending mid-sentence. The last one, dated yesterday, finally finishes: 'I should have said I love you.' Emotional beat: grief and fury and hope colliding; the decade of silence made legible.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the memorial concert, Casper takes the stage he abandoned ten years ago. Mid-piece, he stops, and before two hundred mourners—and Ilse, and Theo holding her hand—he says the sentence he rehearsed for a decade. Emotional beat: climax; terror transfigured into courage, the performance that finally costs him everything worth having.

chapters.title: Everything After
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, epilogue tone. Spring. Ilse didn't choose Casper over Theo so much as honesty over arrangement; Theo, freed, conducts in Vienna and sends them postcards of his own. In a small flat above a rehearsal hall, Casper and Ilse write the first sentence of a new piece together. Emotional beat: resolution; found family, love chosen daily rather than owed.
